pron_note: Never ob-STY-nayt — the stress is right at the front and the ending mumbles away.
means:
Refusing to change your mind, your course, or your behaviour — and refusing past the point where anyone thinks it's reasonable.

The word carries a verdict. *Determined*, *resolute* and *steadfast* describe the same immovability with approval; **obstinate** is what the people you're blocking call it. It implies the resistance has stopped serving any purpose — you're holding out from sheer will, possibly against your own interests. It's also a notch more formal and colder than *stubborn*, which can be affectionate ("stubborn old mule"); obstinate rarely is.

It works on things too: an **obstinate** stain, an **obstinate** cough, an **obstinate** lid — anything that won't yield to repeated effort.
trap: **obstinate ≠ obstreperous.** Both start *obst-*, both describe a difficult person — but **obstinate** is silently immovable, **obstreperous** (ub-STREP-er-uhs) is *noisily* unruly. The obstinate witness says nothing; the obstreperous one won't stop shouting.
trick_line: There's an **obstacle** hiding in **obstinate** — and it's a person.
trick_unpack: Same *obst-*, same idea: this isn't admirable firmness, it's something standing in the way that you've given up trying to move.
sentences: Despite three days of testimony and a mountain of documents, the minister remained **obstinate** in his denial.
He's so **obstinate** — the restaurant's been closed for a year and he still won't admit I was right about the reservation.
in_the_wild: Lady Catherine de Bourgh's parting shot at Elizabeth Bennet in *Pride and Prejudice*: **"Obstinate, headstrong girl!"** — kept word-for-word in the 2005 film. Note who says it: the person being defied, furious that she can't win.
etymology:
Latin **ob-** (*against*) + **stāre** (*to stand*) — literally *to stand against*. The obstinate man plants his feet.

**stāre** is one of the great GRE roots: **stable**, **status**, **stationary**, **constant**, **circumstance**, **obstacle** — everything that stands, stays, or gets in the way.
one_line: Stubborn past the point of reason; immovably set.
